problems: The MCF-7 ChIP-seq results support local occupancy for FOXA1 and GATA3, but do not show that either factor binds the T allele more strongly than the C allele in cells.
The element is called Low-DNase/inactive in MCF-7 (E05), so its distal enhancer-like annotation and factor occupancy do not establish active enhancer function in this context.

TOX3 is the leading candidate target by L2G and has a reported contact in other biosamples, but there is no reported element eQTL or CRISPR perturbation linking this element to TOX3. GTEx found no significant single-tissue eQTL (E09).

The T allele is associated with breast cancer in the strongest reported associations, but the evidence does not connect any candidate factor's allele-sensitive binding to a change in TOX3 or to disease risk. One listed breast-cancer-related association reports C as the effect allele (E07).

checks.why: Independently checks for a Factorbook peak containing the variant for FOXA1 in MCF-7, which could strengthen or weaken the local-occupancy support for H1.
Independently checks for a Factorbook peak containing the variant for GATA3 in MCF-7, which could strengthen or weaken the local-occupancy support for H2.

critique.next_experiment: In a relevant breast-cancer context, perform allele-specific FOXA1 and GATA3 occupancy assays alongside isogenic C-to-T editing, then test factor-dependent effects on TOX3 expression. This would distinguish the best-supported occupancy candidates and test whether the variant affects the proposed target.

lookups.why: Independently checks for a Factorbook peak containing the variant for FOXA1 in MCF-7, which could strengthen or weaken the local-occupancy support for H1.
Independently checks for a Factorbook peak containing the variant for GATA3 in MCF-7, which could strengthen or weaken the local-occupancy support for H2.

games.reason: GATA3 is better supported as the local MCF-7 factor: it is much more highly expressed than MSX2 (346.0 vs 17.6 TPM), has a ChIP-seq summit only 8 bp from the variant, and has multiple MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant. MSX2 also has a nearby summit and both models favor the alt allele, but its summit is farther away and the Homeodomain-family models disagree on direction. The inactive MCF-7 element call and the target-gene and phenotype evidence do not distinguish the chains.

GATA3 is the better-supported member: it is highly expressed in MCF-7, has an in-vitro model favoring the T allele, and has repeated GATA3 ChIP-seq support at the variant, including an MCF-7 summit 8 bp away. MSX2 is expressed and has a nearby summit, but its family models disagree on direction and the screen does not rule out paralogs. The shared gene and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains.
